steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease and flour an 11x13-inch cake pan.

Stir together white cake mix, flour, sugar, and salt in a large bowl until well mixed. Pour in water, sour cream, oil, almond extract, vanilla, and egg whites; beat with an electric mix on low until all the ingredients are mixed and moistened but some lumps still remain, about 4 minutes.
Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is a light golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean, about 25 minutes. Allow to cool before frosting.

raw_recipe.headline: White Almond Wedding Cake
raw_recipe.description: A wonderful white wedding cake recipe. Start with a white cake mix, and add sour cream and almond flavoring to make a cake that's ready to decorate.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to use a package of white cake mix as a base for a wedding-worthy dessert. We sweeten up the cake with extra sugar and flavor it with vanilla and almond extracts. Try baking this cake in round pans and decorate with your favorite frosting or chocolate ganache.

review.reviewBody:
I LOVE this recipe. I make wedding cakes from my home and this is one of my go to recipes. It's a great base recipe that I use adding flavorings and extracts. The most popular one so far is the original recipe, but with vanilla bean along with the almond, and then raspberry preserves whipped with buttercream filling. I also throw in lemon zest and juice (omitting the almond) and orange zest and juice with a honey simple syrup brushed on the baked and cooled cake. This is my favorite cake recipe, great texture, crumb, very moist, but holds up when handling it to make larger wedding cakes. And holds Marshmallow Fondant (found on this site) beautifully. Thank you so so so much for sharing with us!!
 *** Just an update.*** I know several people wonder if this can adapted to a choc cake. I have done this several times now. Here's what I do: I use Duncan Hines Dark Choc Fudge. Instead of 1c flour i use 2/3c flour and 1/3 cocoa powder. I use Ghirardelli. It comes out wonderful. Hope this helps !

This is an absolute keeper. The best white moist cake I have ever tasted. I used a whipped icing and filled layers with pineapple. .I am thinking the next one should have strawberry layers, then trying a lemon cake mix with pineapple the next time. I made this in 3 round cake layers and it took about 38 minutes to bake. So good, don't look any further. This is better than the most expensive cakes I have had at weddings. The secret to a light cake is to mix as directed but add the whipped egg whites to the batter the last minute not with the other ingredients, otherwise, you will have a denser cake, not a light one. Absolutely worthwhile. Been baking over 38 years and this is the best white cake.

NOV 2022- I changed A LOT in this recipe and it still works so the foundation of this recipe is solid. I used 2 whole eggs. I also used milk. I baked at 325 for 25 mins in a standard oven on middle rack. It was maybe a touch doughy at the bottom but overall fully cooked. I also used GLUTEN FREE cake mix and GLUTEN FREE (Bobs red mill) flour. I also only used 1/2 cup of sugar instead of a full cup. My eggs and sour cream were ROOM TEMP. It’s plenty sweet without the extra sugar. It is a denser cake. Which I like because it’s supposed to be wedding cake-esque. It tastes great with the amount of extract they recommend. I did use 18oz of cake mix not just 15 from a standard box. It puffed in middle and sunk on sides but I cut it to even it out before stacking. I put it in two 8 inch tins and one 6 inch tin. I filled with a vanilla custard/pudding and did light dulce de leche frosting with kosher salt all over to cut through sweetness. Also important to note that bake time will differ. I used very thin cakes. If you want a taller cake you might have to cook longer. Just watch with toothpicks. And I think if you want really white color you’d have to stick to egg whites. It was slightly tinged yellow IMO.

I've seen many versions of a cake recipe using a box cake mix. This one was probably fabulous when it was posted with an 18 ounce cake mix, but cake mixes are down to 15.25 ounces, so the ratio of added ingredients needs to be modified. The most important issue that needs to be addressed concerns cook time. I'm not sure how the original recipe has a 25 minute cook time. It is so far off. The most common complaint is everyone stating that the middle of the cake collapsing. The reason that everyone's cake is collapsing is because it is not completely baked. I knew that 25 minutes would never be long enough for my standard 9X13 cake pan and I went to 45 minutes, Even then the middle of mine was still undercooked. One professional baker said that she bakes hers for 60 minutes. For my next cake, I will bake my next one for at least 60 minutes and pro-rate all of the added add in's to the reduced size of the cake mix except the vanilla and almond and add a teaspoon of baking soda to support the extra flour and sugar and 2 teaspoons of almond, 1 teaspoon of vanilla. Also, this first cake turned out good just dumping it all in a bow and mixing for 4 minutes. But next time I will do the correct method of first creaming the sugar, egg whites and sour cream, oil, water first. Then add the dry ingredients. This cake is moist and gives you something to actually bite into other than the standard air you get with regular cake mixes now.

Very good! I followed the recipe completely. I baked it in two 8 inch glass pans and baked for about 35 minutes. I frosted it with a vanilla almond buttercream frosting: (2.5 c. powdered sugar, 1/3 c. butter at room temperature, 1 tsp vanilla, 1/2 tsp. almond extract and 1-2 Tbsp. milk. Beat the butter on medium speed for 1 minute with a hand mixer until smooth. Add the vanilla extract, almond extract. Mix on a low speed until the ingredients are incorporated. Mix the powdered sugar and milk on a low speed.) This frosting only covered the top and sides of the layered cake. The whole cake was gone in two days! Delicious! After trying it, my daughter requested I make this cake for her birthday!

NOTE: The original recipe called for 18.25 oz box of cake mix. Unfortunately, the boxed cake in stores got smaller yet more expensive, but the recipe wasn't adjusted for the other ingredients. Buy a second box of cake mix and take 3 oz out of it. If you use this recipe with 15.25 oz box of cake mix, it won't come out right. I've used this recipe (the original) since 2012. It tastes like Publix cake when you use 18.25 oz of cake mix and all vanilla extract.

I made this recipe for my son's wedding and it was a big hit. I had to alter the ingredients to make it non-dairy, so I used non-dairy sour cream. Before this recipe was updated, it called for a cake mix that was 18.25 oz., but the mix I used came in the 15.25 oz. package. I bought an extra box of mix to add a scant 1/2 cup of additional cake mix to the recipe. This worked. I did find that the cake was probably a little bit more dense with the non-dairy sour cream, so it took longer to bake. I also baked it in round cake pans in order to make a tiered wedding cake. The cake was yummy, and now my daugher wants me to make the same cake for her when she gets married.

I made this recipe and it turned out great. I did use milk instead of water and used two whole eggs instead of the egg yolks. I even used three 8 inch round cake pans. Many ovens are different, which is why I kept an eye on my cakes and toothpick tested them. No complaints here.

I’ve been making this cake for birthdays and weddings since 2016 and it’s perfect every time. My extended family always requests I bring the cake :). I don’t change a thing, except for doubling or tripling depending on number of layers. It’s so versatile. I’ve made it with several different fillings: salted caramel, raspberry, strawberry, lemon, Nutella. (No almond flavoring for the lemon cake). I use the buttercream icing layer then a thin layer of the filling on top of that with a buttercream “dam” to keep it from oozing out, then another cake layer.

This is my go to cake recipe for most all of my cakes and cupcakes. Everyone requests these for all occasions. You can even substitute other flavors of cake mixes. I prefer Betty Crocker brand cake mixes for best results.
I changed and used milk and 2whole eggs instead of all egg whites. No color change. Still tastes amazing. Milk gives a smoother texture. I made for cupcakes.
I made it for my son's wedding for just the 2 of them. I used 3-6" round cake pans and it was perfect. They loved it! I also put a almond buttercream frosting on it.

Love the flavor and ease of this cake. Have made it multiple times, but just made it for the first time in about a year and I always forget that the 25 minute bake time is way off! I bake for 40 and then increase 5-10 minutes as needed.
Absolutely perfect for birthday cupcakes! The texture is spot on and the flavor is subtle but delicious!

I made 3 cakes for a party following the recipe exactly. Absolutely gross. Gummy yet dry, zero flavor except for a raw flour taste. Waste of time and ingredients . Nobody liked it. We threw the leftovers away.

Brought this to work and everyone raved about this cake. My husband and I tested at home first and he made sure I left some at home. I put a raspberry filling between the layers.This is definitely going to be a go to for me
I’ve used this recipe for years and everyone loves it. I freeze my cakes at least a week even longer before I frost and they are always so moist and delicious!
Very moist. I always add an additional tablespoon of extra oil to increase moisture in all cake recipes. Excellent recipe!

I made this for strawberry short cake and it's perfect for that or any other cake 'need'! It's not too sweet and a good level of density. I followed the recipie as written, adding the egg whites to the mixed batter last. The cake is excellent! I put about 1/2 cup of batter into 2 ungreased ramikins (each) so I could sample! They baked in 18 minutes. The rest of the batter was devided into two 9 " pans. They baked in 30 minutes.
Perfect recipe! Love the density of this cake!
